label: Squarish 3BR / baths DISTRIBUTED with central BEDROOM-LOBBY HUB — a small square lobby at the geometric centre of the plan takes all three bedroom doors (br2+br3 paired on one wall, master alone on another) and the common bath's door on a third wall, with its fourth side open to the great_room; zero corridor run. Open-plan great_room + kitchen (gr style).

adjacencies.note: br2 door opens onto the hub; shares its wall (and typically a single jamb post) with the br3 door — two bedroom doors on one wall is the signature move of this parti, confirmed independently in pep_SHD-2015013, pep_DESIGN2 and pep_SHD-2017032.
br3 door pairs with br2's on the same hub wall.
master's only access — a single door on a second hub wall, opposite or adjacent to the br2/br3 pair depending on which corner the master occupies.
ensuite opens directly off master, not off the hub — sanctioned rule-1 arrangement, matching pep_DESIGN2's cleaner version rather than introducing a W.I.C. pass-through.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM 2 OF 3 PRECEDENTS: pep_DESIGN2 and pep_SHD-2015013 both swing the common bath's only door off the kitchen floor, breaking TOPOLOGY_GUIDE rule 1's [HARD] no-toilet-into-kitchen-prep-zone sub-rule (PD 856). pep_SHD-2017032 proves the fix costs nothing: the bath keeps the identical kitchen-adjacent plumbing wall (see the wet_core edge below) but the door leaf swings from the hub side instead. This catalog entry adopts the compliant version as the canonical form.
common bath backs onto the kitchen wall, sharing one plumbing stack — the physical adjacency the flawed precedents got right; only the door side changes.

the hub's fourth side is fully open to the great_room — no wall, no door. This open mouth is what makes it a hub rather than a corridor, and it satisfies the [PREFER] hallway-to-public open_plan rule. Confirmed in all three precedents.

great_room + kitchen read as one open LDK (gr style). Field note: pep_SHD-2017032's kitchen is only semi-open (one wide cased opening) rather than fully open — a legitimate compact variant if the shell is tight, but the canonical entry keeps it fully open plan for consistency with the family's other three gr-style siblings.
full party wall between the paired standards, no opening. Confirmed in all three precedents.
acoustic buffer between the bath and the nearer standard bedroom; no opening.
ensuite's far wall buffers the standard-bedroom band; no opening.

soft_proximities.note: keep the single wet stack tight — common bath and kitchen should land on the same short plumbing run
let the master corner sit toward the entry side so its blind wall doubles as an acoustic buffer for the public room, not an awkward rear pocket

lot_adjustment_profiles.name: compact_sq_bedroom_lobby_hub_baths_ds_hall_gr
lot_adjustment_profiles.rationale: ESTIMATED, not solver-derived (see notes). The hub spends less floor area on circulation than any hallway sibling in the family — pep_SHD-2017032's own note calls it 'zero corridor length spent' — so this may be the family's true compact champion once verified; the 95 sqm trigger is set slightly below front_back_split's 100 sqm as a conservative estimate of that advantage, not a measured threshold.

notes: *** SOLVER-VERIFIED 2026-08-05 (COMPLIANT), WITH ONE AUTHORING BUG FOUND + FIXED ***
Verified by running this file through the actual pipeline code (ai/pipeline.py
_run_hand_authored -> solver/solver.py CP-SAT solve -> core/validator.py) in
floorplan_v1, the same functions the app.py tool calls — not a separate re-
implementation. Confirmed COMPLIANT (0 errors) at: 13.5x13.5 lot / ncp
and 11x12 / ncp (15.79, buildable envelope only 7.0x8.0 m = 56 sqm). A 10x10
lot (6.0x6.0 m = 36 sqm buildable) came back INFEASIBLE — expected: every
sibling in this branch has a stated minimum feasible shell well above that,
so this is a real floor-space floor, not a bug.
THE BUG (now fixed): the file as first drafted declared BOTH a hard adjacency
(master <-> great, kind bedroom_to_public_wall) AND a front_to_rear_stack
["great","hub","master"] that forces hub to sit physically between them.
Those two constraints are mutually exclusive by construction — a room
(hub) with positive depth sitting between great and master makes it
geometrically impossible for great and master to ever touch, so the model
was infeasible at every lot size, including generous ones, not just tight
ones. Confirmed by isolating it: removing that one stack alone (independent
of every other adjacency and of the br2/br3/kitchen stacks, all of which
were individually innocent) flipped the model from infeasible to solvable.
Fix applied: removed the master--great hard adjacency and the
["great","hub","master"] stack entry. The original design intent (master
corner leaning toward the entry side) is kept as the soft_proximity
master<->great below, which the solver honors when it can without it being
a hard requirement.
HUB GEOMETRY vs LOT SIZE — measured 2026-08-05 (supersedes the caveat
this replaces, which had the relationship BACKWARDS). The hub reads as a
true square lobby at the TIGHT end and degrades into a corridor as the
lot GROWS. Measured hub aspect ratio (ncp, all-2.0 m setbacks):
11x11.25  2.20 x 2.15  aspect 1.02   <- true square lobby
15x15     4.80 x 1.20  aspect 4.00   <- pure corridor, parti defeated
The earlier note's '~3.0x2.0, hallway-shaped' reading came from
13.5x13.5 runs only and generalized the wrong way. Treat ~14x14 as the
practical UPPER bound for this parti: above it the solver has enough
slack to stretch the hub into the corridor the design exists to avoid.
The adjacency graph is intact at every size tested (hub keeps all 3
bedroom doors + common bath door + open mouth to great) — it is the
hub's SHAPE that degrades, not its connectivity.
CARPORT (ccp) SIZING — the raw ccp feasibility floor is 12x12
(11.75x11.75 and 11.75x12 both INFEASIBLE; the front-right L-notch costs
roughly 0.75-1 m over the ncp minimum in both dimensions), but 12x12
solves DEGENERATE: hub 4.25 x 1.00 m (aspect 4.25, a 1 m corridor with
five doors opening into it) and ensuite 1.25 x 5.00 m (aspect 4.00),
at 0 hard errors and 0 warnings — the compact profile's hallway
min_least_dim_m of 0.95 is what lets a corridor pass as the lobby.
The published ccp minimum is therefore 12.5x12.5, one notch up, where
the parti reads correctly: hub 2.50 x 1.95 m (aspect 1.28), ensuite a
square 1.95 x 1.95 m, master 13.0 sqm, great_room 17.0 sqm, and every
hub adjacency met with margin. The ccp test brief was re-based
12x12 -> 12.5x12.5 on 2026-08-05 for exactly this reason. If a future
change needs 12x12 ccp to be usable, raise the hallway floor to ~1.5 m
so no size can pass a corridor off as the lobby.
If a guaranteed square lobby at all sizes matters more than the current
solvability band, this needs a hard constraint linking master to the
hub/great cluster (an anchor, or a stack that does NOT sandwich hub
between master and great) — flagged for a follow-up pass, not guessed
at here.
left_anchored/right_anchored remain deliberately null (as originally
authored) — not needed for a feasible solve in any verified run, so no
reason to add them.
lot_adjustment_profile's buildable_area_lt_sqm: 95 threshold is still an
ESTIMATE (see rationale field) — not re-derived from the verification runs
above, which only bracket the real floor somewhere between 36 sqm (fails)
and 56 sqm (solves compliant).
--- original authoring notes below (provenance, unchanged) ---
3BR squarish catalog topology #5 — BEDROOM-LOBBY HUB.
Provenance: 'bedroom_lobby_hub' was coined as a one-off token for a single
plan (pep_SHD-2015013) in the July 2026 precedent-extraction pilot. The
August 2026 full run (53 houses) found it again independently in
pep_DESIGN2 and pep_SHD-2017032 (plus its near-duplicate sibling sheet
pep_SHD-2017032-DESIGN2, and pep_SHD-2015022) — 5 of 53 houses, second only
to side_split in frequency across the whole corpus, and specifically 5 of
the 15 real 1s/3br/squarish leads found in that run. It is a genuine
recurring PH pattern, not a one-off drafting quirk, and this is its first
catalog authoring.
Layout intent as originally drawn (illustrative only — the solver is free to
arrange rooms differently now that master--great is a soft, not hard, link;
see the verified-geometry caveat above for what it actually produced):
| br2   | br3        | common | kitchen    |  rear
| ensuite       |            |              |
| master         |          |                |
|         great_room (entry)                 |  front / street
Program: the hub takes bedroom doors on two of its four sides (br2+br3
paired on one, master alone on another), the common bath's door on a
third, and is fully open to the great_room on the fourth. This is why
zone_split is null: the private rooms wrap the hub on multiple sides
rather than forming a single column, so this parti does not fit the
family's usual two-column vertical/horizontal split model — confirmed
independently in all three source precedents' own parti_notes, which each
separately ruled out side_split, center_spine and half_spine as poor fits
for the same structural reason.
The corrected sanitation issue: 2 of the 3 precedents (pep_DESIGN2,
pep_SHD-2015013) swing the common bath's only door off the kitchen floor,
which breaks TOPOLOGY_GUIDE rule 1's [HARD] PD-856 sub-rule — both rear
bedrooms' occupants would have to cross the open kitchen/food-prep zone to
reach the bath. pep_SHD-2017032 shows this costs nothing to fix: same
shared plumbing wall to the kitchen (kept here as the wet_core edge), door
leaf simply swung from the hub side instead. This catalog entry builds the
compliant version as the default, per TOPOLOGY_GUIDE's own instruction that
the catalog should hold to its stated standard even where market practice
does not.
Fallback: none declared. No sibling in this branch declares fallback_topology
yet either (checked directly against the other four files on 2026-08-05) —
that convention has not been applied to this branch at all so far, not just
to this new entry.
When brief.carport_side='left', mirror the topology (consistent with all
four siblings' convention, not independently verified here).
